methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a local native in Hampton Roads signal grassroots knowledge distribution outside major tech hubs, suggesting peer-to-peer learning networks could enable deep capability in non-metro regions if sustained beyond individual initiatives.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab launch in Southwest Virginia demonstrates institutional commitment to building deep AI literacy in a traditionally underserved region, potentially creating a distributed node of capability if it reaches beyond campus into surrounding communities.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA concentrates institutional resources and expertise in Richmond's urban core, deepening metro capability but success depends on whether 'community impact' extends beyond the city limits into rural Central Virginia.

signals.title: Inside the AI-powered system sorting Hampton Roads' trash - 13newsnow.com
signals.signal_reading: AI-powered trash sorting systems represent shallow, platform-delivered automation that requires minimal local AI fluency—technology adoption without capability building, signaling distribution of AI tools but not AI understanding or development skills.

signals.title: Second Major Virginia Data Center Project Dies, Raising AI Site Selection Stakes - Data Center Knowledge
signals.signal_reading: Data center project failures in NoVA despite its infrastructure advantages reveal that even concentrated tech regions face limits, while continuing data center focus reinforces NoVA's infrastructure concentration without necessarily building distributed AI workforce capability statewide.
